source_event.summary: Independent audit found that client propagation of a selected contract was accepted while the server mutation did not enforce the exact active selected scope.

generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A mutating client can propagate a selected tenant or account scope and look correctly scoped while the server authorizes only the global actor plus resource identifier, allowing a same-actor resource from another scope to cross the intended boundary.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Validate that the actor owns the resource somewhere globally and treat a client header or query parameter as sufficient evidence that the mutation is scoped.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: For a request-selected scope, the server mutation must resolve active authority for that exact scope, bind the target resource to it, and revalidate mutable authority and state inside the commit boundary.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Treat client scope propagation as insufficient authorization evidence; require same-actor different-scope, revoked-authority and concurrent-state sibling cases and re-derive authorization/isolation from restrictive canonical language.

transfer_cases.scenario: One account belongs to two workspaces and supplies an invoice identifier from the non-selected workspace; the server must reject before side effects.
One practitioner identity has two active organizations and supplies a record from the other selected organization; exact-scope authority must be revalidated at commit.
